questions.q: Why does Paine argue that people need society and laws?
a: We depend on others and sometimes make selfish, harmful choices
Without laws, people would naturally cooperate
Society exists mainly to protect private property
Kings are needed to settle disputes fairly
questions.why: Lesson 1 says nobody thrives alone, and because people can be selfish, we need rules to keep them from hurting each other.

questions.q: Which example does the summary use to show how interdependent people are?
a: Many people are involved in making and delivering a lightbulb
A farmer plowing a field without any help
A surgeon operating alone in a hospital
A family deciding where to eat dinner
questions.why: The summary points to the electric company, manufacturer and retailer behind a single lightbulb.

questions.q: Why does Paine prefer elected representatives to a monarchy?
a: Representatives can be replaced and must answer to the people
Elected leaders are better educated than kings
Monarchs cannot pass laws quickly enough
Elections make government cheaper to run
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that elected officials who enact the people's wishes serve society better than a ruler by birthright.

questions.q: Why does Paine say frequent elections matter?
a: They keep officials focused on current issues and accountable
They give more people a chance to hold office
They prevent any one party from forming
They make political campaigns less expensive
questions.why: The summary says repeated polling forces leaders to review and stay current on the most important issues.

questions.q: Why did America need to separate from Britain, according to the summary?
a: It had come of age and Britain ruled it as a tyranny
Britain had stopped trading with the colonies
America wanted to install its own monarchy
The colonies disagreed about who should lead them
questions.why: Lesson 3 compares America to a teenager leaving home and cites unfair taxes and the lack of representation in Parliament.
